statement: Every element carries a renovation status that decides how it appears in views and how it is counted in schedules.
superiority: Status is a typed property with history, so a demolition set can be diffed between design stages.

acceptance.sketch: Set 3 walls to each status: schedule count by status is 3/3/3 and the default status of new elements is New.

notes: VERIFIED — read Renovation; each element has status Existing, To be Demolished or New (default Existing) which drives view display; schedule counting via filtered views (Listing Material Quantities)

statement: Define named renovation filters that choose, for each of the three statuses, whether elements are shown, hidden or overridden with the style of a graphic override rule.
superiority: Filters share the one graphic override rule engine so renovation graphics and custom colour-coding never conflict.

acceptance.sketch: Filter Demolition Plan: existing shown grey, demolished dashed red, new hidden; assert per-status outlines in the plan drawing.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Show/Hide/Override Elements By Renovation Status; per status choose Show, Hide or Override, override style from graphic override rules; filters are saved in the project

statement: Select which renovation filter is active in each view or layout drawing, independent of other views.
superiority: Filter is stored in the view so layouts reproduce exactly in batch publishing.

acceptance.sketch: Two views with different filters show different graphics of the same wall in one session.

notes: VERIFIED — read Apply Renovation Filter and Renovation Filters; filter chosen from quick options or palette and saved with each view

statement: Predefined renovation filters such as existing plan, demolition plan, after demolition and planned status give one-click displays of a chosen subset of statuses.
superiority: Quick modes combine with queries instead of fixed switches.

acceptance.sketch: Applying the existing plan filter hides new elements; applying the planned status filter hides demolished elements.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Examples of Renovation Filters; predefined filters such as Existing Plan, Demolition Plan, After Demolition, Planned Status, Change Plan act as the quick modes

statement: Renovation filters can replace the cut fill of existing or demolished elements with a solid fill so sections show retained, demolished and new structure distinctly.
superiority: Per-skin override within a composite as well as per element.

acceptance.sketch: A section of a demolished wall with solid cut fill active shows a solid fill while a new wall keeps its building material fill.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Additional Renovation Filter Options; solid cut fill option for existing/demolished elements and filter overrides apply in every model view; per-skin overrides not described

statement: Elements can be hidden, shown or overridden by renovation status in plan, section and 3D views via the active filter.
superiority: Hide state recorded in the view for audit.

acceptance.sketch: Hidden status removes elements from plan and 3D but keeps them in schedules.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Show/Hide/Override Elements By Renovation Status and Examples of Renovation Filters; hide or override supported (override style, optional transparent fill); no ghost display described

statement: A palette assigns a renovation status to the selected elements, sets the default status for newly placed elements, and switches the active filter.
superiority: Bulk status change by query with a preview of affected elements.

acceptance.sketch: Selecting a wall and clicking Demolish sets status and records the change.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Renovation Palette and Assign Renovation Status to Elements; palette sets status of the selection and the default for new elements, switches filter and pins an element to one filter; no pick-up/inject tool

statement: Schedule views obey the view's renovation filter, so two component lists with different filters give demolished and new quantities by comparison.

source.ref: Listing Material Quantities for Renovation Projects

superiority: Quantity of demolition and new work in a single comparison view.

acceptance.sketch: Demolition quantity equals the volume of demolished walls to 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Listing Material Quantities for Renovation Projects; schedule views apply renovation filters (Existing Plan vs After Demolition) and their lists are compared; no status criterion field described

statement: Combine renovation status with phase attributes for multi-stage refurbishment.

source.ref: Renovation: Phase management of renovation workflows

superiority: Phases are named ordered stages with status transitions validated.

acceptance.sketch: Phase 2 filter displays status progression per stage.

notes: REJECTED: no AC30 help page describes renovation phases or phase attributes; renovation is limited to the three statuses plus filters (searched 'phase' across help)

statement: Openings in demolished walls take over demolished status by default when the wall status changes.

source.ref: Renovation: Door and window status inheritance

superiority: Inheritance rules are explicit and overridable per type.

acceptance.sketch: Demolishing a wall sets contained door to demolished unless overridden.

notes: REJECTED: Openings By Renovation Status page (050-111) says moved windows are modelled twice with explicit statuses; no automatic status inheritance from wall to opening is described

statement: Library objects follow the renovation filter like other elements, and a demolished-element option can hide them or mark demolished doors and windows with an X symbol.
superiority: Applies to all drawing primitives uniformly.

acceptance.sketch: Dashed override applied to object symbol lines.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Additional Renovation Filter Options; override rules (line type, fill, pens) apply to objects too, with optional hide-objects and X-mark options; no dashed 2D symbol rule specific to objects

statement: Renovation status applies to whole elements only, so changes to parts of an assembly are modelled as separate elements with their own status.
superiority: Part-level status supported.

acceptance.sketch: A wall with a new insulation layer is modelled as the existing wall plus a new element and each carries its own status.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Workflows for Tricky Renovation Situations; status belongs to whole elements, component-level status is not supported so partial changes are modelled as separate elements

statement: Zone stamps carry a renovation status and can be limited to one filter, so existing and planned room data can appear in different filtered views.

source.ref: Zone Stamps for Renovated Rooms: Renovation Workflow

superiority: Zone status derived from boundary elements as an option.

acceptance.sketch: Zone new shows stamp; demolished shows crossed out.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Zone Stamps for Renovated Rooms; zone stamps carry a status and can be pinned to one filter; one stamp cannot express two statuses, so text boxes are used in the interim view

statement: On IFC import, renovation status can be mapped from a custom property, with a configurable fallback status for elements that have none.
superiority: Round trip mapping profile saved with the translator.

acceptance.sketch: Importing an element lacking status with fallback set to New yields renovation status New.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Property Mapping for IFC Import and Using the Mapping Table; renovation status is an import category, with a user-chosen replacement status when the IFC lacks one; custom property mapping is manual

statement: Export renovation status as IFC property or status attribute.
superiority: Standard mapping with bSDD references.

acceptance.sketch: Status appears as Pset_...Status value in IFC.

notes: UNVERIFIED — cached help documents only IFC import handling of renovation status (121-27/28); export-side property naming is not in the cached pages

statement: The same renovation filters apply in 3D, sections and elevations.
superiority: Consistent in every view type.

acceptance.sketch: 3D view with filter hides new elements.

notes: VERIFIED — read Renovation Filters and Graphic Overrides; filter is saved per view and applies to model views including sections; unavailable for drawing-type or manual-rebuild section views

statement: Hotlinked modules keep or override status for their elements.
superiority: Module-level override recorded.

acceptance.sketch: Module status override applied.

notes: REJECTED: no AC30 help page describes keeping or overriding renovation status on hotlinked modules (searched hotlink and renovation pages)

statement: Selecting elements by any method, such as a marquee, and clicking a status sets that status on all selected elements at once.
superiority: Applies by query as well.

acceptance.sketch: A marquee selecting 5 elements followed by the To Be Demolished action sets 5 elements to that status.

notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Assign Renovation Status to Elements; status is applied to the current selection by clicking a palette icon, however the selection was made

statement: Keep an existing-condition model as reference from point cloud or scan, then new design on top.

source.ref: Renovation: Existing model reference for surveys

superiority: Point clouds are first-class reference geometry.

acceptance.sketch: Imported scan mesh is displayed as existing reference geometry.

notes: REJECTED: the Renovation chapter (050-101..118) does not describe point-cloud or scan baselines; Point Clouds (120-33) are a separate interoperability feature that mentions renovation only as a use case

statement: Publisher sets output views with their assigned renovation filters.
superiority: Filter travels with the saved view in all outputs.

acceptance.sketch: PDF page uses filter of its view.

notes: VERIFIED — read Renovation Filters; the filter is saved with the view so it also affects drawings placed in documentation; Publisher outputs views and layouts as they appear

statement: An element can be restricted to a single renovation filter so it exists visibly only in that filter, provided its status would normally be shown there.

source.ref: Show an Element in a Single Renovation Filter Only

superiority: Pinned elements are listed and flagged in one overview.

acceptance.sketch: A pinned new element is visible in the planned filter and absent from the demolition filter.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Show an Element in a Single Renovation Filter Only; set from palette or element settings

statement: A reset command at the end of a renovation remaps all elements' statuses in all views, for example new to existing, demolished to deleted, with elements pinned to a filter handled only if visible in the target filter.
superiority: Reset is previewed with counts and creates a restore point.

acceptance.sketch: Resetting new to existing leaves no element with status new and the count of existing rises by the former new count.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Reset Renovation Status; needs show-all-elements option to reach pinned elements

statement: Renovation filter options can be duplicated, renamed, deleted and exported or imported as XML, and are stored with the project so a template carries them.
superiority: Filter libraries are versioned and shareable across a firm.

acceptance.sketch: Exporting a filter and importing it in a clean project reproduces its settings for all three statuses.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Renovation Filter Options and Best Practices for Creating Renovation Views; XML export/import, saved in template

statement: Extra override options for existing and demolished elements include hiding opening dimension markers, solid or transparent cut fill, hiding zones, objects and opening symbols, and marking demolished openings with an X.
superiority: Each option previews its effect on a sample wall.

acceptance.sketch: With hide objects on in the demolition filter, objects with status demolished disappear from the plan.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Additional Renovation Filter Options; also do-not-intersect and opening infill contours as demolished

statement: Annotation elements such as dimensions, texts, labels, drafting fills, lines and markers can be excluded from renovation overrides so only model elements change appearance.
superiority: Exclusions are per annotation class with live preview.

acceptance.sketch: With do-not-override-dimensions on, a dimension of a demolished wall keeps its normal pen.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Additional Renovation Filter Options; checkboxes for dimensions/texts/labels, drafting fills/lines, markers

statement: A default status for elements placed later can be set from the palette when nothing is selected, so new work in an existing project gets the new status automatically.
superiority: Default status follows the active filter so new work cannot get the wrong status.

acceptance.sketch: With the default set to New, a newly drawn wall has status New and existing walls keep Existing.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Assign Renovation Status to Elements and Renovation Palette; default is Existing until changed
